partition_policy.training: all target facts except source-exclusive validation and blind facts

results.name: Comorbidity-constrained shared-target indication transfer
results.hypothesis: A treated indication can transfer to a clinically coexisting disease when the drug inhibits a causal gene shared by both diseases.
results.body: training-treated anchor coexists with candidate; drug inhibits causal gene shared by anchor and candidate
results.mechanism_rationale: The rule combines a shared molecular mechanism with clinical co-occurrence, but coexistence is SemMedDB-derived and does not imply shared therapeutic direction.
results.trapi_notes: The positive paths are TRAPI-expressible; source exclusion, shared-target identity, and ontology constraints require post-processing.
results.cypher:
MATCH (subject:Drug)-[treatment:TREATS|AMELIORATES_CONDITION]->(anchor:Disease)
WHERE any(
  source IN coalesce(treatment.primary_knowledge_sources, [])
  WHERE NOT source IN ['infores:drug-repurposing-hub', 'infores:ttd']
)
MATCH (anchor)-[:COEXISTS_WITH]-(object:Disease)
MATCH (subject)-[:DIRECTLY_PHYSICALLY_INTERACTS_WITH]->(gene:Gene)
MATCH (subject)-[effect:AFFECTS]->(gene)
MATCH (gene)-[:MINER_GENE_DISEASE_EVIDENCE]->(anchor)
MATCH (gene)-[:MINER_GENE_DISEASE_EVIDENCE]->(object)
WHERE object <> anchor
  AND effect.qualified_predicate = 'biolink:causes'
  AND effect.object_aspect_qualifier = 'activity_or_abundance'
  AND effect.object_direction_qualifier = 'decreased'
  AND coalesce(object._miner_disease_descendant_degree, 0) <= 500
  AND object._miner_disease_superclass_degree >= 1
  AND object.id STARTS WITH 'MONDO:'
RETURN DISTINCT subject.id AS subject_id, object.id AS object_id

results.name: Dual-target comorbidity-constrained indication transfer
results.hypothesis: Comorbidity-constrained transfer is more credible when the drug inhibits at least two causal genes shared by the treated anchor and candidate disease.
results.body: R144 with at least two distinct shared inhibited causal genes
results.mechanism_rationale: The two-target mechanism is stronger than coexistence alone, but observed coverage is dominated by broad cancer-to-breast-cancer transfer.
results.trapi_notes: The positive paths are TRAPI-expressible; two-target cardinality, source exclusion, identity, and ontology constraints require post-processing.
results.cypher:
MATCH (subject:Drug)-[treatment:TREATS|AMELIORATES_CONDITION]->(anchor:Disease)
WHERE any(
  source IN coalesce(treatment.primary_knowledge_sources, [])
  WHERE NOT source IN ['infores:drug-repurposing-hub', 'infores:ttd']
)
MATCH (anchor)-[:COEXISTS_WITH]-(object:Disease)
MATCH (subject)-[:DIRECTLY_PHYSICALLY_INTERACTS_WITH]->(gene:Gene)
MATCH (subject)-[effect:AFFECTS]->(gene)
MATCH (gene)-[:MINER_GENE_DISEASE_EVIDENCE]->(anchor)
MATCH (gene)-[:MINER_GENE_DISEASE_EVIDENCE]->(object)
WHERE object <> anchor
  AND effect.qualified_predicate = 'biolink:causes'
  AND effect.object_aspect_qualifier = 'activity_or_abundance'
  AND effect.object_direction_qualifier = 'decreased'
  AND coalesce(object._miner_disease_descendant_degree, 0) <= 500
  AND object._miner_disease_superclass_degree >= 1
  AND object.id STARTS WITH 'MONDO:'
WITH subject, object, count(DISTINCT gene) AS gene_count
WHERE gene_count >= 2
RETURN subject.id AS subject_id, object.id AS object_id
